sections.heading: How they differ
paragraphs: Case Western Reserve University vs George Washington University (CWRU vs GWU) differ primarily in size and location. CWRU, located in Cleveland, has an undergraduate enrollment of 6,437 students, whereas GWU in Washington enrolls 11,182 undergraduates. Both institutions are private nonprofit universities, as indicated by College Scorecard ownership code 2. Tuition costs for in-state students are comparable, with CWRU charging $66,608 and GWU slightly higher at $67,710. These distinctions highlight differences in campus environment and scale between the two universities.

sections.heading: Cost
paragraphs: Cost is a significant factor when comparing Case Western Reserve University vs George Washington University (CWRU vs GWU). Both universities charge similar tuition rates for in-state and out-of-state students, with CWRU's tuition set at $66,608 and GWU's slightly higher at $67,710. Despite the close tuition figures, the median debt for students who complete their degrees differs between the two institutions. Graduates from CWRU carry a median debt of $24,000, whereas those from GWU have a lower median debt of $20,449. These financial metrics provide insight into the economic considerations prospective students might evaluate when choosing between CWRU vs GWU.
